The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary, so that $M$ is Hausdorff
and second countable and carries a maximal smooth atlas
([[def-smooth-manifold]]). Let $g$ be a smooth covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$
in the sense of [[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]. Then $g$ assigns
to every $p\in M$ a bilinear form $g_p:T_pM\times T_pM\to\mathbb R$
([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]).

**(a) Lorentzian metric.** The field $g$ is a **Lorentzian metric of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$** on $M$ when it is symmetric and nondegenerate, and at every
$p\in M$ the pair $(T_pM,g_p)$ is a Lorentz vector space of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ in

Use the signature $(-,+,+,+)$ throughout. In the flat case, **Minkowski spacetime** means the affine model $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ of [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]: $A$ is an affine space, $\eta$ is a nondegenerate Lorentz form on its four-dimensional displacement space, and $C^+$ selects the future cone. In the curved case, a **background spacetime** means a prescribed smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]; the metric and time orientation are fixed data, not dynamical unknowns here. No field equation or completeness assumption is included.

A **massive worldline** on an open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ is a $C^2$ curve $x:I\to M$ with future-directed timelike tangent $T=dx/ds$ at every parameter value. This is the smooth subclass of [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]. A **null worldline** is a $C^2$ curve with nonzero future-directed null tangent everywhere. Its tangent has no proper-time normalization: $g(T,T)=0$, so the massive proper-time formula does not apply. In the flat model these are affine curves into $A$ with tangent in the selected future timelike or null cone from [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]].

An **observer at an event** $p\in M$ is a future unit timelike vector $n\in T_pM$ with $g_p(n,n)=-1$, as in [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]. Its instantaneous rest space is $n^\perp=\{v:g_p(v,n)=0\}$. This is a pointwise vector-space construction; the definition does not assign a clock reading or a moving frame to a lone observer.

An **observer congruence** on an open set $U\subseteq M$ is a smooth field of future unit timelike vectors on $U$, as in [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]; its observer curves are its integral curves. A **tetrad** is a chosen orthonormal frame field, as in [[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]. A **chart** is a coordinate map; an adapted chart is a chart whose spatial coordinates are constant along the congruence's integral curves. These objects are distinct: a chart need not be inertial, a tetrad need not be coordinate induced, and a congruence is a field of observers rather than a chart or a frame. This distinction agrees with [[def-sr-chart-tetrad-and-congruence-distinction]].

The coordinates and units used later are SI: in an inertial chart $x^0=ct$ and $x^i$ are metres, $t$ is seconds, $c>0$ is metres per second, and proper time is measured in seconds. In a general chart, coordinate components inherit their coordinate units; invariant equations are tensorial. No global inertial chart, global tetrad, or global observer congruence is asserted to exist.

Let $F:M^m\to N^n$ be smooth, let $q\in N$ be a regular value, and assume
$F^{-1}(q)$ is nonempty. Then $F^{-1}(q)$ is an embedded submanifold of
codimension $n$. Equivalently, it has dimension $m-n$.

Let $L(q,v)$ be $C^2$ on a conic open subset of a tangent bundle, and suppose $L(q,av)=aL(q,v)$ for every $a>0$ in its domain. At each nonzero $v$,

$$v^iL_{v^i}=L,\qquad L_{v^iv^j}v^i=0,\qquad E_L:=v^iL_{v^i}-L=0.$$

Consequently the velocity Hessian is singular and the fibre derivative cannot be a local diffeomorphism there; a regular Legendre equivalence theorem cannot be applied. These conclusions do not imply that the motion is static or that the Lagrangian has a specified constraint surface.

Let $\eta$ be a Lorentz form on a $4$-dimensional real vector space $V$. There
is an ordered basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of $V$ with
$\eta(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$ for all $a,b$. Such a basis
is called **$\eta$-orthonormal**; in every $\eta$-orthonormal ordered basis
exactly one basis vector is timelike and the other three are spacelike, and the
count is the inertia $(3,1,0)$ of $\eta$.

Let $c > 0$ and let $(A,V,\eta,C^{+})$ be an oriented time-oriented affine
Minkowski space ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]).

**(a) Norm of the four-velocity.** Let $x : I \to A$ be a $C^{1}$ future
timelike worldline with four-velocity $U$
([[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]). Then
$\eta(U(s),U(s)) = -c^{2}$ for every $s \in I$; equivalently the dimensionless
four-velocity $u = U/c$ satisfies $\eta(u,u) = -1$, and $U(s)$ is future
timelike. Thus the dimensionless four-velocity lies on the future unit
hyperboloid $\{v \in C^{+}:\eta(v,v)=-1\}$.

**(b) Orthogonality of the four-acceleration.** If $x$ is $C^{2}$ at $s$, then
$\eta(U(s),A(s)) = 0$: the four-acceleration has no component along the
four-velocity; if in addition $A(s) \ne 0$, then $A(s)$ is spacelike.

**(c) Rest space and projection.** Let $n \in V$ be future unit timelike,
$\eta(n,n) = -1$, and put $n^{\perp} := \{\,v \in V : \eta(n,v) = 0\,\}$
([[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]). Then $n^{\perp}$ is a
3-dimensional linear subspace of $V$, the restriction of $\eta$ to $n^{\perp}$
is positive definite, and the map $h : V \to V$, $h(v) := v + \eta(n,v)\,n$, is
linear, idempotent with $h \circ h = h$, has image $n^{\perp}$ and kernel
$\operatorname{span}(n)$, satisfies $h(n) = 0$ and $\eta(n,h(v)) = 0$ for all
$v \in V$, and every $v \in V$ has the unique decomposition
$v = -\eta(n,v)\,n + h(v)$. Moreover $|w| := \sqrt{\eta(w,w)}$ defines a norm
on $n^{\perp}$.

**(d) Relative velocity and Lorentz factor.** Let $n$ and $u$ be future unit
timelike vectors, put $\gamma := -\eta(n,u)$ and $w := c\,h(u)/\gamma$. Then
$\gamma \ge 1$, $w$ lies in $n^{\perp}$,
$u = \gamma\,(n + w/c)$, $|w|^{2} = c^{2}(1-\gamma^{-2}) < c^{2}$,
$\gamma = (1-|w|^{2}/c^{2})^{-1/2}$, and $\gamma = 1$ if and only if $u = n$.
The vector $w$ is the velocity of a worldline with four-velocity $cu$ relative
to the observer $n$, and $\gamma$ is its Lorentz factor.

**(e) Coordinate form.** Let $(o;e_0,\dots,e_3)$ be an inertial frame and let
$y$ be a $C^{1}$ future timelike worldline whose inertial coordinates are
$t \mapsto (ct,r(t))$, with coordinate velocity $w(t) := r'(t)$ in
$\mathbb{R}^{3}$ and, when $y$ is $C^{2}$, coordinate acceleration
$a(t) := w'(t)$. Then $|w(t)| < c$, the four-velocity is
$U = \gamma_w\,(c,w)$ with $\gamma_w := (1-|w|^{2}/c^{2})^{-1/2}$, and the
four-acceleration is $A = \gamma_w\,\frac{d}{dt}\bigl(\gamma_w(c,w)\bigr)$, so
that

$$A^{0} = \gamma_w^{4}\,\frac{w \cdot a}{c}, \qquad A_{\mathrm{vec}} = \gamma_w^{2}\,a + \gamma_w^{4}\,\frac{(w \cdot a)\,w}{c^{2}} ;$$

consequently
$\eta(A,A) = \gamma_w^{4}|a|^{2} + \gamma_w^{6}(w \cdot a)^{2}/c^{2} \ge 0$,
with $\eta(A,A) = 0$ if and only if $a = 0$, and $\eta(U,A) = 0$. For the
observer $n = e_0$ of the chart, clauses (c) and (d) specialize to
$\gamma = \gamma_w$ and $w_{\mathrm{rel}} = (0,w)$ in the frame coordinates, identified with $w$ via the spatial basis.

**(f) Scope.** The statement is a theorem about the affine Minkowski model with
a fixed positive constant $c$; it asserts no clock reading and identifies no
physical four-velocity. No choice principle is used.

derivations.claim: Use the supplied smooth tangent/cotangent bundle structure under [A1] and the Lorentzian data [F1]. Differentiate $L=-mc\sqrt{-g_{ij}V^iV^j}$ with respect to $V^a$. Because $s>0$, ordinary chain rule gives $p_a=mcV_a/s$. Differentiating again gives $L_{V^aV^b}=mc(g_{ab}/s+V_aV_b/s^3)$.

Contract the Hessian with $V^b$: $mc(V_a/s+V_a g(V,V)/s^3)=0$, since $g(V,V)=-s^2$. For $W\perp_g V$, contraction with $W$ has quadratic value $(mc/s)g(W,W)$. The normalized vector $u=V/s$ is future unit timelike by [F2]; [F5] identifies this tangent Lorentz space with the standard Lorentz vector space, and [F6] makes its orthogonal complement positive definite. Thus the Hessian is positive on every nonzero $W\perp_g V$, so its kernel is precisely $\mathbb RV$ and its rank is three.

The momentum in step 1.1 satisfies $g^{-1}(p,p)=(mc/s)^2g(V,V)=-m^2c^2$ and is future because it is a positive multiple of $V^\flat$. Conversely, for any future covector on this shell, set $V=p^\sharp$. Then $s=mc$, and the same formula returns $p$; every positive multiple of $V$ returns the same covector. This proves exact image and positive-ray fibres.

The defining function $C=\tfrac12(g^{-1}(p,p)+m^2c^2)$ has fibre differential $d_pC=p^\sharp\ne0$ on the shell. By [F3] the shell is embedded. The Legendre map fixes the base point and has fibre differential of rank three by step 1.2, so its differential has rank $4+3=7$, the shell dimension; it is a submersion onto that image.
Euler's identity from [F4] gives $p(V)-L=0$, while the nonzero kernel direction in step 1.2 rules out a local diffeomorphism and any four-velocity inverse.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Assume
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).
For this general metric define $\flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot)$,
$\sharp_p:=\flat_p^{-1}$, and
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta)$.
Nondegeneracy makes $\flat_p$ injective and hence invertible between the
four-dimensional tangent space and its dual. In a chart, $g^{ab}$ are the
entries of the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab})$. These definitions agree with
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]] in its Lorentzian scope.
Here and below repeated upper/lower indices are summed over $0,1,2,3$.
This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth local vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

with brackets as in [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]].

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth local }X,Y,Z .$$

It is torsion-free and $g$-compatible, so it is a metric-selected connection
for $(M,g)$, meaning torsion-free and satisfying
$Xg(Y,Z)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$ for smooth local fields
(the conditions of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] extended here to
nondegenerate $g$); in every smooth chart its
Christoffel symbols are

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

with $g^{ad}$ the inverse-metric components defined above
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**(c) Induced derivative on tensor fields.** Let $\nabla^*$ be the dual
connection on $T^*M$ and let the product connection of
[[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]] act on
$T^r_sM:=(TM)^{\otimes r}\otimes(T^*M)^{\otimes s}$, for integers $r,s\ge0$,
constructed by [[lem-finite-tensor-products-of-smooth-vector-bundles]]. A
type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$ is a multilinear map
$(T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s\to\mathbb R$
([[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]); a smooth
tensor field is a section with smooth coefficients in each local product
frame. The empty product is the scalar line. Its chart components are
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}=T(dx^{a_1},\ldots,dx^{a_r},\partial_{b_1},\ldots,\partial_{b_s})$,
where $dx^a$ is dual to $\partial_a$. This agrees with
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] in the Lorentzian case. Put
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}:=(\nabla_{\partial_c}T)^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}$.
Then, in every smooth chart, for
every smooth tensor field $T$ of type $(r,s)$,

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

Let $M$ be a smooth manifold without boundary with affine connection $\nabla$, and let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with nonempty interior. A smooth curve $\gamma:I\to M$ is an **affinely parametrized geodesic** when
$$D_t\gamma'(t)=0\qquad(t\in I),$$
with one-sided interpretation at an included endpoint. Constant curves are geodesics. Unless another parametrization is explicitly stated, “geodesic” means affinely parametrized geodesic.

For a given connection on $E$ and a smooth curve on an interval with nonempty interior, the **covariant derivative along the curve** is
$$D_tV=(\gamma^*\nabla)_{\partial/\partial t}V.$$
Here $V$ is a section of the pullback bundle as in [[def-vector-field-and-section-along-a-smooth-curve]], and the pullback connection exists by [[thm-pullback-connection-is-well-defined-and-functorial]]. It is real-linear and satisfies $D_t(fV)=f'V+fD_tV$ for functions of the parameter.

At an included endpoint the smooth up-to-boundary coefficients have their one-sided derivative; equivalently any smooth local extension of the coefficients gives this value, because extensions agreeing on a one-sided interval have the same derivative there. For a piecewise smooth curve the derivative is defined on each piece, with separate one-sided derivatives at corners; those derivatives are not required to agree. A singleton interval carries no derivative operator under this convention and will have identity transport by definition. A zero section or a rank-zero bundle gives zero covariant derivative. Constant base curves can have sections with nonzero coefficient derivative.

Let $(O,\mathcal L)$ be a time-dependent Lagrangian chart over $[a,b]\times U$ in the sense of
[[def-cm-time-dependent-lagrangian-and-action]] and let $q:[a,b]\to U$ be a $C^2$ admissible curve.
Then $q$ is stationary for the action $S$ if and only if

$$E_{\mathcal L}(q)(t)=0\qquad\text{for every }t\in[a,b].$$

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$ and let $(M^{2n},\omega)$ be a smooth symplectic manifold. A finite family of smooth functions $\chi_1,\ldots,\chi_r$ defined on an open neighborhood $U\subseteq M$ is a **regular primary constraint family** on

$$C:=\{z\in U:\chi_1(z)=\cdots=\chi_r(z)=0\}$$

when $d\chi_1(z),\ldots,d\chi_r(z)$ are linearly independent at every $z\in C$. The regular-level theorem [[thm-a-regular-level-set-is-an-embedded-submanifold]] then gives $C$ its embedded-submanifold structure and $T_zC=\bigcap_a\ker d\chi_a(z)$. For functions $F,G$ on $U$, write $F\approx G$ when $F|_C=G|_C$; thus $F\approx0$ means that $F$ vanishes on $C$, without requiring it to vanish off $C$.

Given a smooth canonical Hamiltonian $H_c$ on $U$ and multiplier functions $u^a(t)$, the **total generator** is

$$H_T(t,z):=H_c(t,z)+\sum_{a=1}^r u^a(t)\chi_a(z).$$

The functions $u^a$ are independent parameter functions; the definition does not assert that their equations determine them. If $H_c$ is an energy and $\chi_a$ has units \([\chi_a]\), then $u^a$ has units energy divided by \([\chi_a]\), so every term in $H_T$ has the same units. A later constraint, if generated by consistency, is not declared primary by this definition.

$$X_H=\frac{\partial H}{\partial p_i}\frac{\partial}{\partial q^i}-\frac{\partial H}{\partial q^i}\frac{\partial}{\partial p_i},\qquad \{F,G\}=F_{q^i}G_{p_i}-F_{p_i}G_{q^i}.$$

The bracket is coordinate independent and makes smooth functions a Poisson algebra. If $H_t$ is smooth on an open time-dependent domain $D\subset\mathbb R\times T^*Q$, each solution of $\dot z=X_{H_t}(z)$ has local uniqueness and smooth dependence on initial data and parameters; on its actual interval,

$$\frac{d}{dt}F(t,z(t))=\partial_tF+\{F,H_t\}.$$

No completeness or global flow is asserted. If $H$ is smooth, each local time-$t$ flow map preserves ω.

In a spacetime chart, variation in $e$ gives $C_m=0$. Variation in $p_a$ gives $x'^a=e g^{ab}p_b$. Variation in $x^a$, integrating the $p_a\delta x'^a$ term by parts with $\delta x$ vanishing at endpoints, gives $p'_a=-e\partial_a C_m=-\tfrac e2\partial_a g^{bc}p_bp_c$. The vertical differential of $C_m$ is $d_pC_m=p^\sharp$; it is nonzero on the massive branch because $g^{-1}(p,p)=-m^2c^2<0$, and on the massless branch because $p\ne0$ and $g^{-1}$ is nondegenerate. Thus the shell is a regular primary constraint by [F7], and [F8] fixes the canonical sign convention. The equations are tensorial and hence agree across overlapping charts.

For $m>0$, the first equation gives $p_a=g_{ab}x'^b/e$. The constraint gives $g(x',x')=-e^2m^2c^2$, so $s=\sqrt{-g(x',x')}=emc$ because $e,m,c>0$. Hence $p_a=mc\,g_{ab}x'^b/s$, the fibre derivative of the square-root Lagrangian; this agrees with the exact image result [F9].

Substituting $p_a=g_{ab}x'^b/e$ into the integrand gives $L_1=g(x',x')/(2e)-em^2c^2/2=-s^2/(2e)-em^2c^2/2$, where $s=\sqrt{-g(x',x')}>0$. Its $e$-derivative is $s^2/(2e^2)-m^2c^2/2$, whose unique positive zero is $e=s/(mc)$; the second derivative there is $-s^2/e^3\ne0$. Thus the $p$- and $e$-stationarity equations determine a unique smooth auxiliary pair $(p^*(x,x'),e^*(x,x'))$ on the future timelike domain, and the stationary integrand is $-mc\,s$. For any fixed-endpoint variation $x_\varepsilon$, choose $p_\varepsilon,e_\varepsilon$ by these formulas. The chain rule for the varied action has the $x_\varepsilon$ variation plus terms proportional to its $p$- and $e$-derivatives; those terms vanish at the auxiliary stationary pair. Hence the first variation of the reduced action equals the $x$-part of the first-order variation. Conversely every stationary first-order triple must equal this unique auxiliary pair, so the same identity gives the reverse implication. This proves the equivalence with the square-root action.

Differentiate $p_a=g_{ab}x'^b/e$, use the second equation, and use the inverse-metric identity $\partial_a g^{bc}g_{bi}g_{cj}=-\partial_a g_{ij}$. Multiplying by $e$ gives
$$g_{ab}x''^b+(\partial_cg_{ab})x'^cx'^b-\frac{e'}e g_{ab}x'^b=\frac12(\partial_ag_{ij})x'^ix'^j.$$
Since $x'^cx'^b$ is symmetric, the difference of the metric-derivative terms is $\frac12(\partial_cg_{ab}+\partial_bg_{ac}-\partial_ag_{bc})x'^cx'^b=g_{ad}\Gamma^d{}_{cb}x'^cx'^b$. Inverting $g_{ab}$ therefore gives
$$\nabla_{x'}x'=\frac{e'}e x'.$$
This computation uses [F3]–[F5]; it is the coordinate form of the reparameterized geodesic equation.

For $m>0$, $d\tau=s\,d\lambda/c=em\,d\lambda$, so $e=1/m$ in proper-time parameter and step 2.1 becomes $\nabla_UU=0$; the converse follows by reversing the momentum definition and the same identities.

For $m=0$, [F2] selects $p\ne0$ future null; the first equation makes $x'=e p^\sharp$, so $x'$ is nonzero future null and the constraint is null. Choose a new parameter σ with $d\sigma/d\lambda=e/e_0$ for any constant $e_0>0$; the connection transformation law applied to step 2.1 gives $\nabla_{dx/d\sigma}(dx/d\sigma)=0$. Since $g(x',x')=0$, the massive proper-time construction cannot be used.

Assume countable choice ACω, as in [[def-countable-choice]], for the smooth cotangent-bundle carrier convention used by this page; no full Axiom of Choice is assumed.

Let $\mathcal D$ be an open subset of the time-dependent tangent bundle $\mathbb R\times TQ$ of a finite-dimensional smooth manifold $Q$, and let $L:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R$ be smooth. For fixed $t$, the **fibre derivative** is the map

$$\mathbb F L(t,q,v)=(t,q,p),\qquad p(w)=\left.\frac{d}{ds}\right|_{s=0}L(t,q,v+sw),$$

as in [[def-fibre-derivative-and-legendre-transform-of-a-lagrangian]]. In induced coordinates $p_i=\partial L/\partial v^i$.

The Lagrangian is **regular** at $(t,q,v)$ when the velocity Hessian $(\partial^2L/\partial v^i\partial v^j)$ is invertible there; regularity gives only a local inverse branch. It is **hyperregular on a declared domain** when $\mathbb F L$ is a diffeomorphism from that entire domain onto an open subset of $\mathbb R\times T^*Q$.

It is **almost regular on a declared domain $\mathcal D_0\subseteq\mathcal D$** when the following are all assumed: $\mathbb F L|_{\mathcal D_0}$ has constant rank; its image $N$ is an embedded submanifold of $\mathbb R\times T^*Q$; its corestriction $\mathcal D_0\to N$ is a surjective submersion (its differential is surjective at every point); and every fibre of that corestriction is connected. These hypotheses are not consequences of singularity alone.

In this relativistic-particle model, $m>0$ is a fixed **primitive mass parameter** measured in kilograms, and $c>0$ is a fixed **primitive conversion parameter** measured in metres per second. They are parameters of the adopted physical formulation, not quantities derived by this definition. where $n^\flat=g(n,\cdot)$. The restriction of $g^{-1}$ to covectors annihilating $n$ is positive definite, so it supplies the norm of $q_n(p)$. Assume countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$: every sequence of nonempty sets has a choice function ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $Q$ be a finite-dimensional, Hausdorff, second-countable smooth manifold without boundary, of dimension $n$. Its cotangent bundle is

$$T^*Q=\coprod_{q\in Q}T_q^*Q,\qquad \pi:T^*Q\to Q,\quad \pi(q,p)=q,$$

with the canonical smooth structure and induced cotangent charts supplied by the manifold construction in [[def-tautological-one-form-on-a-cotangent-bundle]]. The **tautological one-form** is $\theta_{(q,p)}(\xi)=p(d\pi_{(q,p)}\xi)$, and the **canonical cotangent two-form** is $\omega=-d\theta$. The exact theorem [[thm-the-canonical-cotangent-two-form-is-symplectic]] makes $(T^*Q,\omega)$ a symplectic manifold in the sense of [[def-symplectic-form-and-symplectic-manifold]]. We call this pair the **cotangent phase space** of $Q$.

In an induced chart $(q^1,\ldots,q^n,p_1,\ldots,p_n)$, $\theta=p_i\,dq^i$ and $\omega=dq^i\wedge dp_i$. A mathematical **observable** on this phase space means a smooth function $F:T^*Q\to\mathbb R$; this definition does not assert that a measurement has been performed or that every such function is physically measurable.

For an interpreted particle model, assign coordinates $q^i$ their declared units and assign the conjugate covector components $p_i$ units of action divided by the units of $q^i$. Thus $\theta$ and $\omega$ have action units, conventionally joule-seconds, and a bracket of quantities with units \([F]\) and \([G]\) has units \([F][G]/(\text{action})\). These are dimensional interpretations of the model, not additional mathematical premises. The use of $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$ is exactly the use in the smooth cotangent-bundle suppliers; no full Axiom of Choice is used.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$ and let $(M^{2n},\omega)$ be a smooth symplectic manifold. A finite family of smooth functions $\chi_1,\ldots,\chi_r$ defined on an open neighborhood $U\subseteq M$ is a **regular primary constraint family** on

$$C:=\{z\in U:\chi_1(z)=\cdots=\chi_r(z)=0\}$$

when $d\chi_1(z),\ldots,d\chi_r(z)$ are linearly independent at every $z\in C$. The regular-level theorem [[thm-a-regular-level-set-is-an-embedded-submanifold]] then gives $C$ its embedded-submanifold structure and $T_zC=\bigcap_a\ker d\chi_a(z)$. For functions $F,G$ on $U$, write $F\approx G$ when $F|_C=G|_C$; thus $F\approx0$ means that $F$ vanishes on $C$, without requiring it to vanish off $C$.

Given a smooth canonical Hamiltonian $H_c$ on $U$ and multiplier functions $u^a(t)$, the **total generator** is

$$H_T(t,z):=H_c(t,z)+\sum_{a=1}^r u^a(t)\chi_a(z).$$

The functions $u^a$ are independent parameter functions; the definition does not assert that their equations determine them. If $H_c$ is an energy and $\chi_a$ has units \([\chi_a]\), then $u^a$ has units energy divided by \([\chi_a]\), so every term in $H_T$ has the same units. A later constraint, if generated by consistency, is not declared primary by this definition.

Use the signature $(-,+,+,+)$ throughout. In the flat case, **Minkowski spacetime** means the affine model $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ of [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]: $A$ is an affine space, $\eta$ is a nondegenerate Lorentz form on its four-dimensional displacement space, and $C^+$ selects the future cone. In the curved case, a **background spacetime** means a prescribed smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]; the metric and time orientation are fixed data, not dynamical unknowns here. No field equation or completeness assumption is included.

A **massive worldline** on an open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ is a $C^2$ curve $x:I\to M$ with future-directed timelike tangent $T=dx/ds$ at every parameter value. This is the smooth subclass of [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]. A **null worldline** is a $C^2$ curve with nonzero future-directed null tangent everywhere. Its tangent has no proper-time normalization: $g(T,T)=0$, so the massive proper-time formula does not apply. In the flat model these are affine curves into $A$ with tangent in the selected future timelike or null cone from [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]].

An **observer at an event** $p\in M$ is a future unit timelike vector $n\in T_pM$ with $g_p(n,n)=-1$, as in [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]. Its instantaneous rest space is $n^\perp=\{v:g_p(v,n)=0\}$. This is a pointwise vector-space construction; the definition does not assign a clock reading or a moving frame to a lone observer.

An **observer congruence** on an open set $U\subseteq M$ is a smooth field of future unit timelike vectors on $U$, as in [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]; its observer curves are its integral curves. A **tetrad** is a chosen orthonormal frame field, as in [[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]. A **chart** is a coordinate map; an adapted chart is a chart whose spatial coordinates are constant along the congruence's integral curves. These objects are distinct: a chart need not be inertial, a tetrad need not be coordinate induced, and a congruence is a field of observers rather than a chart or a frame. This distinction agrees with [[def-sr-chart-tetrad-and-congruence-distinction]].

The coordinates and units used later are SI: in an inertial chart $x^0=ct$ and $x^i$ are metres, $t$ is seconds, $c>0$ is metres per second, and proper time is measured in seconds. In a general chart, coordinate components inherit their coordinate units; invariant equations are tensorial. No global inertial chart, global tetrad, or global observer congruence is asserted to exist.

$$T^*Q=\coprod_{q\in Q}T_q^*Q,\qquad \pi:T^*Q\to Q,\quad \pi(q,p)=q,$$

with the canonical smooth structure and induced cotangent charts supplied by the manifold construction in [[def-tautological-one-form-on-a-cotangent-bundle]]. The **tautological one-form** is $\theta_{(q,p)}(\xi)=p(d\pi_{(q,p)}\xi)$, and the **canonical cotangent two-form** is $\omega=-d\theta$. The exact theorem [[thm-the-canonical-cotangent-two-form-is-symplectic]] makes $(T^*Q,\omega)$ a symplectic manifold in the sense of [[def-symplectic-form-and-symplectic-manifold]]. We call this pair the **cotangent phase space** of $Q$.

In an induced chart $(q^1,\ldots,q^n,p_1,\ldots,p_n)$, $\theta=p_i\,dq^i$ and $\omega=dq^i\wedge dp_i$. A mathematical **observable** on this phase space means a smooth function $F:T^*Q\to\mathbb R$; this definition does not assert that a measurement has been performed or that every such function is physically measurable.

For an interpreted particle model, assign coordinates $q^i$ their declared units and assign the conjugate covector components $p_i$ units of action divided by the units of $q^i$. Thus $\theta$ and $\omega$ have action units, conventionally joule-seconds, and a bracket of quantities with units \([F]\) and \([G]\) has units \([F][G]/(\text{action})\). These are dimensional interpretations of the model, not additional mathematical premises. The use of $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$ is exactly the use in the smooth cotangent-bundle suppliers; no full Axiom of Choice is used.

$$C:=\{z\in U:\chi_1(z)=\cdots=\chi_r(z)=0\}$$

$$H_T(t,z):=H_c(t,z)+\sum_{a=1}^r u^a(t)\chi_a(z).$$

The functions $u^a$ are independent parameter functions; the definition does not assert that their equations determine them. If $H_c$ is an energy and $\chi_a$ has units \([\chi_a]\), then $u^a$ has units energy divided by \([\chi_a]\), so every term in $H_T$ has the same units. Use the signature $(-,+,+,+)$ throughout. In the flat case, **Minkowski spacetime** means the affine model $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ of [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]: $A$ is an affine space, $\eta$ is a nondegenerate Lorentz form on its four-dimensional displacement space, and $C^+$ selects the future cone. In the curved case, a **background spacetime** means a prescribed smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]; the metric and time orientation are fixed data, not dynamical unknowns here. No field equation or completeness assumption is included.

A **massive worldline** on an open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ is a $C^2$ curve $x:I\to M$ with future-directed timelike tangent $T=dx/ds$ at every parameter value. This is the smooth subclass of [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]. A **null worldline** is a $C^2$ curve with nonzero future-directed null tangent everywhere. Its tangent has no proper-time normalization: $g(T,T)=0$, so the massive proper-time formula does not apply. In the flat model these are affine curves into $A$ with tangent in the selected future timelike or null cone from [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]].

An **observer at an event** $p\in M$ is a future unit timelike vector $n\in T_pM$ with $g_p(n,n)=-1$, as in [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]. Its instantaneous rest space is $n^\perp=\{v:g_p(v,n)=0\}$. This is a pointwise vector-space construction; the definition does not assign a clock reading or a moving frame to a lone observer.

An **observer congruence** on an open set $U\subseteq M$ is a smooth field of future unit timelike vectors on $U$, as in [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]; its observer curves are its integral curves. A **tetrad** is a chosen orthonormal frame field, as in [[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]. A **chart** is a coordinate map; an adapted chart is a chart whose spatial coordinates are constant along the congruence's integral curves. These objects are distinct: a chart need not be inertial, a tetrad need not be coordinate induced, and a congruence is a field of observers rather than a chart or a frame. This distinction agrees with [[def-sr-chart-tetrad-and-congruence-distinction]].

The coordinates and units used later are SI: in an inertial chart $x^0=ct$ and $x^i$ are metres, $t$ is seconds, $c>0$ is metres per second, and proper time is measured in seconds. In a general chart, coordinate components inherit their coordinate units; invariant equations are tensorial. No global inertial chart, global tetrad, or global observer congruence is asserted to exist.

Let $\mathcal D$ be an open subset of the time-dependent tangent bundle $\mathbb R\times TQ$ of a finite-dimensional smooth manifold $Q$, and let $L:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R$ be smooth. For fixed $t$, the **fibre derivative** is the map

It is **almost regular on a declared domain $\mathcal D_0\subseteq\mathcal D$** when the following are all assumed: $\mathbb F L|_{\mathcal D_0}$ has constant rank; its image $N$ is an embedded submanifold of $\mathbb R\times T^*Q$; its corestriction $\mathcal D_0\to N$ is a surjective submersion (its differential is surjective at every point); and every fibre of that corestriction is connected. These hypotheses are not consequences of singularity alone.

$$T^*Q=\coprod_{q\in Q}T_q^*Q,\qquad \pi:T^*Q\to Q,\quad \pi(q,p)=q,$$

with the canonical smooth structure and induced cotangent charts supplied by the manifold construction in [[def-tautological-one-form-on-a-cotangent-bundle]]. The **tautological one-form** is $\theta_{(q,p)}(\xi)=p(d\pi_{(q,p)}\xi)$, and the **canonical cotangent two-form** is $\omega=-d\theta$. The exact theorem [[thm-the-canonical-cotangent-two-form-is-symplectic]] makes $(T^*Q,\omega)$ a symplectic manifold in the sense of [[def-symplectic-form-and-symplectic-manifold]]. We call this pair the **cotangent phase space** of $Q$.

In an induced chart $(q^1,\ldots,q^n,p_1,\ldots,p_n)$, $\theta=p_i\,dq^i$ and $\omega=dq^i\wedge dp_i$. A mathematical **observable** on this phase space means a smooth function $F:T^*Q\to\mathbb R$; this definition does not assert that a measurement has been performed or that every such function is physically measurable.

For an interpreted particle model, assign coordinates $q^i$ their declared units and assign the conjugate covector components $p_i$ units of action divided by the units of $q^i$. Thus $\theta$ and $\omega$ have action units, conventionally joule-seconds, and a bracket of quantities with units \([F]\) and \([G]\) has units \([F][G]/(\text{action})\). These are dimensional interpretations of the model, not additional mathematical premises. $$C:=\{z\in U:\chi_1(z)=\cdots=\chi_r(z)=0\}$$

when $d\chi_1(z),\ldots,d\chi_r(z)$ are linearly independent at every $z\in C$. The regular-level theorem [[thm-a-regular-level-set-is-an-embedded-submanifold]] then gives $C$ its embedded-submanifold structure and $T_zC=\bigcap_a\ker d\chi_a(z)$. $$H_T(t,z):=H_c(t,z)+\sum_{a=1}^r u^a(t)\chi_a(z).$$

The functions $u^a$ are independent parameter functions; the definition does not assert that their equations determine them. If $H_c$ is an energy and $\chi_a$ has units \([\chi_a]\), then $u^a$ has units energy divided by \([\chi_a]\), so every term in $H_T$ has the same units. Use the signature $(-,+,+,+)$ throughout. In the flat case, **Minkowski spacetime** means the affine model $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ of [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]: $A$ is an affine space, $\eta$ is a nondegenerate Lorentz form on its four-dimensional displacement space, and $C^+$ selects the future cone. In the curved case, a **background spacetime** means a prescribed smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]; the metric and time orientation are fixed data, not dynamical unknowns here. No field equation or completeness assumption is included.

A **massive worldline** on an open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ is a $C^2$ curve $x:I\to M$ with future-directed timelike tangent $T=dx/ds$ at every parameter value. This is the smooth subclass of [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]. A **null worldline** is a $C^2$ curve with nonzero future-directed null tangent everywhere. Its tangent has no proper-time normalization: $g(T,T)=0$, so the massive proper-time formula does not apply. In the flat model these are affine curves into $A$ with tangent in the selected future timelike or null cone from [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]].

An **observer at an event** $p\in M$ is a future unit timelike vector $n\in T_pM$ with $g_p(n,n)=-1$, as in [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]. Its instantaneous rest space is $n^\perp=\{v:g_p(v,n)=0\}$. This is a pointwise vector-space construction; the definition does not assign a clock reading or a moving frame to a lone observer.

An **observer congruence** on an open set $U\subseteq M$ is a smooth field of future unit timelike vectors on $U$, as in [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]; its observer curves are its integral curves. A **tetrad** is a chosen orthonormal frame field, as in [[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]. A **chart** is a coordinate map; an adapted chart is a chart whose spatial coordinates are constant along the congruence's integral curves. These objects are distinct: a chart need not be inertial, a tetrad need not be coordinate induced, and a congruence is a field of observers rather than a chart or a frame. This distinction agrees with [[def-sr-chart-tetrad-and-congruence-distinction]].

The coordinates and units used later are SI: in an inertial chart $x^0=ct$ and $x^i$ are metres, $t$ is seconds, $c>0$ is metres per second, and proper time is measured in seconds. In a general chart, coordinate components inherit their coordinate units; invariant equations are tensorial. No global inertial chart, global tetrad, or global observer congruence is asserted to exist.

A mathematical **observable** on this phase space means a smooth function $F:T^*Q\to\mathbb R$; this definition does not assert that a measurement has been performed or that every such function is physically measurable.

Thus $\theta$ and $\omega$ have action units, conventionally joule-seconds, and a bracket of quantities with units \([F]\) and \([G]\) has units \([F][G]/(\text{action})\). No field equation or completeness assumption is included.

A **massive worldline** on an open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ is a $C^2$ curve $x:I\to M$ with future-directed timelike tangent $T=dx/ds$ at every parameter value. This is the smooth subclass of [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]. A **null worldline** is a $C^2$ curve with nonzero future-directed null tangent everywhere. Its tangent has no proper-time normalization: $g(T,T)=0$, so the massive proper-time formula does not apply. In the flat model these are affine curves into $A$ with tangent in the selected future timelike or null cone from [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]].

An **observer at an event** $p\in M$ is a future unit timelike vector $n\in T_pM$ with $g_p(n,n)=-1$, as in [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]. Its instantaneous rest space is $n^\perp=\{v:g_p(v,n)=0\}$. This is a pointwise vector-space construction; the definition does not assign a clock reading or a moving frame to a lone observer.

An **observer congruence** on an open set $U\subseteq M$ is a smooth field of future unit timelike vectors on $U$, as in [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]; its observer curves are its integral curves. A **tetrad** is a chosen orthonormal frame field, as in [[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]. A **chart** is a coordinate map; an adapted chart is a chart whose spatial coordinates are constant along the congruence's integral curves. These objects are distinct: a chart need not be inertial, a tetrad need not be coordinate induced, and a congruence is a field of observers rather than a chart or a frame. This distinction agrees with [[def-sr-chart-tetrad-and-congruence-distinction]].

The coordinates and units used later are SI: in an inertial chart $x^0=ct$ and $x^i$ are metres, $t$ is seconds, $c>0$ is metres per second, and proper time is measured in seconds. In a general chart, coordinate components inherit their coordinate units; invariant equations are tensorial. No global inertial chart, global tetrad, or global observer congruence is asserted to exist.

$$v^iL_{v^i}=L,\qquad L_{v^iv^j}v^i=0,\qquad E_L:=v^iL_{v^i}-L=0.$$

The velocity Hessian is $mc(g_{ab}/s+V_aV_b/s^3)$, has kernel exactly $\mathbb RV$, and rank three. The image consists exactly of the future shell $\Sigma_m^+=\{(x,p)\in T^*M:g_x^{-1}(p,p)=-m^2c^2,\ p^\sharp\text{ future}\}$. Each fibre is a connected positive ray, and the Legendre map is a surjective submersion onto this embedded image. Its energy $p(V)-L$ is zero; the map has no local inverse in the four-velocity direction.

In affine Minkowski space with $x^0=ct$, let $m\ge0$, $p_i$ be spatial momentum components and $p_i\ne0$ for $m=0$. On the future shell, $p_0=-E/c$, where

$$E(\mathbf p)=\sqrt{m^2c^4+c^2|\mathbf p|^2}.$$

On any compact interval $J=[t_1,t_2]$ of inertial time, the gauge $x^0=ct$ reduces the first-order shell action to

$$I_J=\int_{t_1}^{t_2}\left(p_i\dot q^i-E(\mathbf p)\right)dt,\qquad q^i=x^i.$$

The gauge pair $C_m=0$, $\psi=x^0-ct=0$ is second class because $\{C_m,\psi\}=-P^0\ne0$ on the future shell; its Dirac reduction gives the canonical spatial bracket. The reduced Hamilton equations are $\dot q^i=c^2p_i/E$, $\dot p_i=0$, agreeing with the unreduced characteristic trajectories. On this full flat future shell every characteristic line meets each inertial-time slice once; this global assertion does not extend by this proof to a curved temporal chart.
